Q: AVAudioPlayer cannot be initialized A:

My root cause was the file was missing in my actual package. When following the suggestion from @SushiHangover to use FromData I got a more clear exception mentioning the file is missing instead of the same message as OP's message.

In my case I converted my Xamarin.iOS application to a .Net MAUI project (the new SDK style) by creating a new project and convert it manually.
As part of the migration I dragged the Sounds directory with all sound files into the new project, but the location of my Sounds was not part of the Resources directory.

In the original Xamarin.iOS project all sound files were added with Build action Content.
In the new .Net MAUI all sound files are not included in the package unless:

  • Set Build action to BundleResource

  • Or drag the directory Sounds to the Resources directory. In the new SDK style project for .Net MAUI all files in Resources seem to be treated as BundleResource without the requirement to explicitly set each Build Action to BundleResource.

Q: How should an app gracefully handle passkey deletion? A:

TL;DR (Apple-approved reality)

You cannot reliably detect from iOS that a passkey was deleted.
You must treat failed authorization as a signal to recover, not as a precise error condition.

Apple does not expose a “passkey deleted” error by design.

Why this happens (important context)

With ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredentialProvider:

  • iOS does not validate credential existence until the user interacts with the system UI

  • If the credential is gone:

    • iOS shows fallback UI (QR code, Chrome, etc.)

    • No explicit error is returned to your app

  • Your stored credentialID becomes stale, but you’re never told

This is intentional to:

  • Preserve privacy

  • Avoid credential enumeration

  • Allow silent syncing between devices/providers

So detection is indirect only.

What Apple expects you to do

1️⃣ Assume passkeys are ephemeral

Treat passkeys like OAuth tokens — they can disappear anytime.

Never assume:

  • A stored credential ID is valid

  • A previous successful registration still exists

2️⃣ Handle authorization failure as a recovery trigger

When authentication fails or returns no credential:

func authorizationController(
    controller: ASAuthorizationController,
    didCompleteWithError error: Error
) {
    // Do NOT retry passkey immediately
    // Do NOT loop authorization
    triggerRecoveryFlow()
}

Even if:

  • error is .canceled

  • or .unknown

  • or nothing useful

👉 Treat it as “passkey unavailable”

3️⃣ Clear local passkey state immediately

If authentication doesn’t return a credential:

func triggerRecoveryFlow() {
    // 1. Remove stored credential ID
    Keychain.delete("passkeyCredentialID")

    // 2. Mark user as "needs re-registration"
    userDefaults.set(true, forKey: "needsPasskeySetup")

    // 3. Show recovery UI
    showRecoveryScreen()
}

This is critical.
Keeping a stale credential ID guarantees dead ends.

4️⃣ Always offer a fallback auth method

Apple expects one of these to exist:

  • Email magic link

  • OTP (SMS / email)

  • Password (even if hidden)

  • App-specific recovery code

UX pattern Apple uses internally:

“Your passkey is no longer available. Continue with another sign-in method.”

After fallback success → re-register passkey automatically.

5️⃣ Re-register passkey silently after fallback login

Once user is authenticated again:

if userJustRecovered {
    promptForPasskeyCreation()
}

Best UX:

  • Explain briefly

  • One-tap re-enable

  • No deep technical wording

What you should NOT do ❌

❌ Don’tWhyRetry authorizationiOS won’t re-prompt properlyInspect credential IDsApple gives no validity checkBlock loginPasskeys are optional by designAssume QR = successIt often leads nowhere

Recommended UX copy (important)

Passkey unavailable
This passkey was removed from your device.
Continue with another sign-in method to restore access.

This matches Apple’s Human Interface Guidelines tone.

Apple’s official stance (implicit)

Apple has intentionally not provided:

  • A “credential exists” API

  • A “passkey deleted” error

  • A validation endpoint

Because:

  • Passkeys sync

  • Providers change

  • Devices come and go

Apps must recover, not detect.

Final recommended architecture

Best practice flow

Try passkey
   ↓
Success → login
   ↓
Failure / fallback UI → recovery
   ↓
Fallback auth (OTP / email)
   ↓
Re-register passkey

This is exactly how:

  • iCloud Keychain

  • Apple ID

  • Safari passkeys
    behave internally.
